title: Record the review of phase 5: three findings, fixed
message:
Record the review of phase 5: three findings, fixed

The review of MR !28 found a stale sheath slot read through freed memory,
a sheathed artifact's destruction unseen by the ledger, and delete_object()
destroying a deleted sheath's weapons and walking into one freed. The
record lists the three fix commits, their tests, the otransform defect
found on the way (#34), and the verification on the last fix commit.

title: Hand a deleted sheath's weapons to its holder
message:
Hand a deleted sheath's weapons to its holder

delete_object() gives a deleted instance's contents to its room, its
wearer or carrier, or the object around it before extracting it, since
extract_obj() would take them along. The sheathed weapons were not given
over: since extract_obj() follows the sheath slots, deleting a sheath's
prototype destroyed every weapon sheathed in a live instance, and when the
weapon created just before the sheath was one of them, the walk over
object_list resumed on it freed.

The sheathed weapons now go over with the contents, by the same places.
An instance that is nowhere keeps what it holds for the extraction, as
before.

Test_gameplay_object_delete_hands_a_sheaths_weapons_to_its_wearer creates
two daggers and then the sheath, sheathes both with the sheath command and
deletes the sheath's prototype: the wearer carries both daggers, out of any
sheath, renumbered onto the chain of the remaining prototype, and
object_list is as it was. Without the change the daggers are destroyed,
and valgrind reports the walk reading the freed off-hand dagger.

title: Count a sheathed artifact's destruction in the artifact ledger
message:
Count a sheathed artifact's destruction in the artifact ledger

artifact_on_extract() takes an object with no holder for a temporary
prototype clone and leaves the ledger alone. A sheathed artifact has no
holder but its sheath, so its destruction, with the sheath junked or sold
or the sheath's prototype deleted, left the player as owner with the
instance marked persisted and no instance anywhere, and every zone reset
refused the zone's copy. A sheathed object now counts as placed: the
check runs before extract_obj() clears the slot, and the sheath's own
extraction reaches the weapon with the back-pointer intact.

Test_artifact_integration_sheathed_instance_destruction_releases_ownership
claims an artifact, sheathes it and destroys it: the ownership is released,
the destruction counted, and a zone reset may put it back. Without the
change the ledger keeps the owner and the reset stays refused.

title: Clear a sheath's slot when its sheathed object is extracted
message:
Clear a sheath's slot when its sheathed object is extracted

A sheathed object has no holder: only its sheath's slot points at it, and
nothing cleared the slot when the object left on its own. delete_object()
extracts every instance of a deleted prototype, and the point update
extracts an object whose timer runs out, a sheathed one included; the
sheath then kept the freed address, and its own extraction, which now
follows the slots, read the freed block and could extract whatever object
had reused it.

A sheathed object now knows its sheath: obj_to_sheath() sets the slot and
the back-pointer together, where sheath and the player sheath loader fill
a slot, and obj_from_sheath() clears both, where unsheath draws an item
and where extract_obj() takes an object out of wherever it is. The two
copies of a live object, overwrite_object() and otransform, keep the
target's sheath links with its other holder links. objs_from_sheath() had
no caller and goes; #33 keeps the loader's debug trace.

Test_gameplay_sheathed_weapon_extracted_alone_leaves_its_slot sheathes a
blade and a shield with the sheath command, extracts the blade alone and
finds the slot empty; the sheath's extraction then takes the shield and
leaves object_list as it was. On the code before this change the slot
keeps the blade and valgrind reports the read of the freed block.
Test_player_load_puts_a_sheaths_weapons_back_in_it saves a loaded sheath
and loads it back through the sheath rows: both weapons are in the sheath
and know it. The unsheath accounting in TestArmCountUnsheathChecksEachItem
checks the back-pointer, set while sheathed and cleared when drawn.

title: Record phase 5 of the object save fixes: built, in review as MR !28
message: Record phase 5 of the object save fixes: built, in review as MR !28

title: Test that a refused weapon row fails the pet save
message:
Test that a refused weapon row fails the pet save

A pet save is all or nothing, and the previous commit gives it two more
records to write. Test_pet_save_stores_a_sheaths_weapons_as_its_own now
refuses the blade's row and then the shield's: each attempt fails the
save and leaves the records written before it.

title: Save a sheath's weapons as a pet's own objects
message:
Save a sheath's weapons as a pet's own objects

A sheath's weapons are stored under their owner's name, in
player_save_objs_sheathed, and a pet has no rows there:
objsave_save_obj_record_db_pet() wrote no sheath rows, so a loaded
sheath given to a pet came back empty when the pet was restored, and
its weapons were in no row.

Crash_save_pet() now writes a sheath's weapons as the pet's own objects
beside the sheath, as House_save() does for a house: no new table and
no migration. A worn sheath's weapons are written as inventory records,
at MIN(0, location), since pet_object_graph_valid() refuses two records
on one wear position, and with them the whole set. The restored pet
carries the weapons and an empty sheath.

title: Extract a sheath's weapons with the sheath
message:
Extract a sheath's weapons with the sheath

A sheath's weapons hang off sheath_primary and sheath_secondary, and
nothing else holds them. extract_obj() did not look at them: junking or
selling a loaded sheath, and the extraction after a rent save, freed the
sheath and left the weapons in object_list with no holder. After a rent
save their rows were written, so they were a leak only; after a junk or
a sale they were gone from play without having been destroyed.

extract_obj() now extracts what a sheath holds, as it does a container's
contents. The weapons stayed on their rnum hash chain, so the memory
checkers never counted them as lost: the new test watches object_list.
Test_house_save_stores_a_sheaths_weapons_as_its_own no longer extracts
its weapons by hand before the teardown extracts the sheath.
